background_notes.fact: For real mean-zero f in H^gamma with gamma>0, f_m=P_{<=m}f is a real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, ||f_m||_{H^gamma}<=||f||_{H^gamma}, ||f||_2<=||f||_{H^gamma}, and ||f_m-f||_2 tends to zero.

grounds.reason: Reality and zero mean are expressed by conjugate symmetry and the zero Fourier coefficient.
The weighted Fourier norm is a convergent nonnegative series and defines the projections.
gamma>0 makes every weight <k>^{2 gamma} at least one.
The chosen u0 has the stated regularity, reality, mean and norm bound.

background_notes.justification: The symmetric finite cutoff preserves conjugate symmetry and deletes no required zero-mode condition. Its weighted norm sum is a sub-sum of the original. The L2 tail is bounded by the tail of the convergent weighted series, which tends to zero. Finite Fourier sums are smooth.

background_notes.fact: P and P0 are bounded on H^s. Dinv, defined to vanish at zero, maps H^s continuously into H^{s+1}, and D^(-2) maps H^s into H^{s+2}, for every real s. Dinv and D^(-2) preserve reality and have zero-mean output even when the input has nonzero mean.

grounds.reason: Sobolev norms are weighted Fourier sums.
The inverse derivative multipliers and their zero-mode convention are supplied.

background_notes.justification: Projection deletes terms of a nonnegative norm sum. At integer k!=0, <k>^2/k^2<=2 and <k>^4/k^4<=4, proving the two multiplier bounds directly. The symbols at -k are conjugates of those at k; the zero output coefficient is zero. Thus the same bounds apply to intermediate products without any mean-zero assumption on those products.

background_notes.fact: The scalar map f -> P0(f^2) is continuous on L2, with |P0(f^2)-P0(g^2)| <= (||f||_2+||g||_2)||f-g||_2. For fixed positive tau all endpoint terms defining F_tau and H_tau are continuous L2 maps. Their sum Psi_tau maps the mean-zero L2 subspace into itself, preserves real inputs, and has continuous finite iterates.

grounds.reason: L2 has the normalized spatial norm.
F_tau consists of projected squares of inverse derivatives and unitary multipliers.
H_tau consists of the four displayed endpoint/product terms with finite coefficients for tau>0.
Psi_tau is their sum with S_tau.
N005 supplies unitary S_t, Dinv:L2->H^1 on mean-zero inputs, and the bounded H^1 product.
The argument fixes tau>0 and considers finitely many iterates.

background_notes.justification: Cauchy-Schwarz applied to (f-g)(f+g) proves the scalar bound and integrability of f^2. A bounded bilinear map is continuous because A(f,f)-A(g,g)=A(f-g,f)+A(g,f-g). Repeated application handles H^1 products and cubes. The Fourier multiplier bounds in BG002 allow every inverse derivative, including those on nonzero-mean products. Thus F_tau maps continuously to H^1; every H_tau term does as well: products of H^1 factors, the continuous scalar mean times an H^1 factor, the cubic endpoint followed by Dinv, and the F_tau-times-inverse-derivative endpoint followed by D^(-2). All endpoints involve fixed real times. For real inputs each operation preserves reality. Zero mean follows from P in the first terms, outer inverse derivatives in the endpoint terms, and the zero-mean S_tau Dinv f factor in the scalar term. Continuity of each finite iterate follows by induction and composition on this invariant subspace.

background_notes.fact: For a fixed finite grid {t_0,...,t_L}, if x_m(t_n)->x(t_n) and y_m^n->y^n in L2 and ||x_m(t_n)-y_m^n||_2<=K for every m,n, then max_{0<=n<=L}||x(t_n)-y^n||_2<=K. No convergence uniform in L or tau is required.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the exact solution convergence.
F002 supplies continuity of finite iterates at each fixed positive timestep.
N011 supplies the same K=C*tau^gamma for every smooth approximant.
L is fixed before taking m to infinity and tau=T/L is positive.

background_notes.justification: At each n the triangle inequality bounds the limiting error by ||x-x_m||_2+K+||y_m^n-y^n||_2. Letting m tend to infinity gives an error at most K. Taking a maximum over the finite grid preserves that bound. N011 chose C,tau0 using only T,gamma,R, so repeating this reasoning for each allowed L and datum does not change those constants.
